582:
(a) The storage, collection and disposal of refuse in the mobile home park or travel trailer parking area shall be so conducted as to create no health hazards, rodent harborage, insect breeding areas, accident or fire hazards or air pollution.
(b) All refuse shall be stored in fly-tight, watertight, rodent-proof containers, which shall be located not more than 150 feet from any mobile home or travel trailer lot. Containers shall be provided in sufficient number and capacity to properly store all refuse.
(c) Refuse collection stands shall be provided for all refuse containers. Such container stands shall be so designed as to prevent containers from being tipped, to minimize spillage and container deterioration and to facilitate cleaning around them.
(d) All refuse containing garbage shall be collected at least twice weekly. Where suitable collection service is not available from municipal or private agencies, the mobile home park or travel trailer parking operator shall provide this service. All refuse shall be collected and transported in covered vehicles or covered containers.
(e) Where municipal or private disposal service is not available, the mobile home park or travel trailer parking area operator shall dispose of the refuse by incineration or transporting to a disposal site approved by the health authority.
(f) Refuse incinerators shall be constructed in accordance with engineering plans and specifications which shall be reviewed and approved by the health authority or other authority having jurisdiction.
(g) Incinerators shall be operated only when attended by some person specifically authorized by the owner or operator of the mobile home park or travel trailer parking area.
(Code 1987, § 10-111; Ord. No. 2012-004, 3-15-2012)
583:
(a) Parks shall be maintained free of accumulations of debris which may provide rodent harborage or breeding places for flies, mosquitoes and other pests.
(b) Storage areas shall be so maintained as to prevent rodent harborage; lumber, pipe and other building material shall be stored at least one foot above the ground.
(c) Where the potential for insect and rodent infestation exists, all exterior openings in or beneath any structure shall be appropriately screened with wire mesh or other suitable materials.
(Code 1987, § 10-112; Ord. No. 2012-004, 3-15-2012)
584:
(a) Park management.
(1) The person to whom a permit for a mobile home park or travel trailer parking area is issued shall operate the park in compliance with this article and regulations issued hereunder and shall provide adequate supervision to maintain the park or area, its facilities and equipment in good repair and in a clean and sanitary condition.
(2) The park or area management shall notify park or area occupants of all applicable provisions of this article and inform them of their duties and responsibilities under this article and regulations issued hereunder.
(3) The park or area management shall supervise the placement of each mobile home or travel trailer stand which includes securing its stability and installing all utility connections.
(4) The park or area management shall maintain a register containing the names of all park or area occupants. Such register shall be available to any authorized person inspecting the park or area.
(5) The park or area management shall notify the health authority immediately of any suspected communicable or contagious disease within the park or area.
(b) Park or area occupants.
(1) The park or area occupant shall comply with all applicable requirements of this article and regulations issued hereunder and shall maintain his mobile home lot or travel trailer parking space, its facilities and equipment in good repair and in a clean and sanitary condition.
(2) The park or area occupant shall be responsible for proper placement of his mobile home or travel trailer on its stand and proper installation of all utility connections in accordance with the instructions of the park management.
(3) No owner or person in charge of a dog, cat, or other pet animal shall permit it to run at large or to commit any nuisance within the limits of any mobile home lot or travel trailer parking space, and all dogs and cats shall have up-to-date rabies vaccinations.
(Code 1987, § 10-113; Ord. No. 2012-004, 3-15-2012)

(c) It shall be the duty of the owners or occupants of mobile home parks or travel trailer parking areas, and mobile homes or travel trailers contained therein, or of the person in charge thereof, to give the health authority free access to such premises at reasonable times for the purpose of inspection.

606:
Subject to provisions of this article the creating of any unreasonably loud, disturbing and unnecessary noise in the unincorporated area of the county is prohibited. Noise of such character, intensity or duration as to be detrimental to the life or health of any individual, or in disturbance of the public peace and welfare is prohibited.
(Code 1987, § 12-50; Ord. of 12-7-1993, § 1)
607:
The following acts, among others, are declared to be loud, disturbing and unnecessary noise in violation of this article; but this enumeration shall not be deemed to be exclusive, namely:
(1) Blowing horns. The sounding of any horn or signal device on any automobile, motorcycle, bus or other vehicle while not in motion except as a danger signal if another vehicle is approaching, apparently out of control, or if in motion, only as a danger signal after or as brakes are being applied and deceleration of the vehicle is intended; the creation by means of any such signal device of any unreasonably loud or harsh sound; and the sounding of such device for an unnecessary and unreasonable period of time.
(2) Radios, phonographs, etc. The playing of any radio, phonograph, or any musical instrument or sound device, including but not limited to loudspeakers or other devices for reproduction or amplification of sound, either independently of or in connection with motion pictures, radio or television, in such a manner or with such volume, particularly during the hours between 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m., as to annoy or disturb the quiet, comfort, or repose of persons in any office or hospital, or in any dwelling, hotel, or other type of residence, or of any person in the vicinity.
(3) Yelling, shouting, hooting, etc. Yelling, shouting, hooting, whistling, or singing on the public streets, particularly between the hours of 11:00 p.m. and 7:00 a.m. or at any time or place so as to annoy or disturb the quiet, comfort, or repose of any persons in any hospital, dwelling, hotel, or other type of residence, or of any persons in the vicinity.
(4) Use of vehicle. The use of any automobile, motorcycle, streetcar, or vehicle so out of repair, so loaded, or in such a manner as to cause loud and unnecessary grating, grinding, rattling, or other noise.
(5) Blowing whistles. The blowing of any steam whistle attached to any stationary boiler, except to give notice of the time to begin or stop-work or as a warning of fire or danger, or upon request of proper county authorities.
(6) Exhaust discharge. The discharge into the open air of the exhaust of any steam engine, stationary internal-combustion engine, motor vehicle, or boat engine, except through a muffler or other device which will effectively prevent loud or explosive noises therefrom.
(7) Noises near schools, hospitals, churches, etc. The creation of any excessive noise on any street adjacent to any hospital or adjacent to any school, institution of learning, church, or court, while in session.
(8) Noises to attract attention. The use of any drum, loudspeaker or other instrument or device emitting noise for the purpose of attracting attention, unless a permit for the use of such device shall have been obtained under the regulations hereinafter provided.
(9) Loudspeaker or amplifiers on vehicles. The use of mechanical loudspeakers or amplifiers on trucks or other moving or standing vehicles for any purposes, unless a permit for the use of such device shall have been obtained under the regulations hereinafter provided.
(Code 1987, § 12-51; Ord. of 12-7-1993, § 2)
608:
(a) The reasonable use of amplifiers, loudspeakers, drums, or other instruments or devices emitting noise for the purpose of any public address or for the purpose of attracting attention to any performance, show, sale or display of merchandise shall be permitted providing a permit therefor is secured from the county administrator. An application for the use desired shall be submitted in writing to the county, which application shall set out the nature of the noise-making activity, the place or places where the activity is to be carried on, and the dates and hours during which the use is to be made. The county administrator shall act upon each application so submitted, and shall, before granting a permit, place such restrictions upon the use as to the extent, hours and location as to prevent undue annoyance to the public or any resident.
(b) The county administrator may, in his discretion, authorize the issuance of certain types of permits by the county without the application being referred to the county administration; but in the case of any doubt, the county shall await action by the county administrator before issuance of a permit. It shall be unlawful to use any device or to create any undue noise in violation of the terms of any permit issued under this section.
(Code 1987, § 12-52; Ord. of 12-7-1993, § 3)

616:
Whenever a written request for inspection is filed with the county by a public authority, by at least five residents of the county or by the public officer charging that any dwelling, building or structure is unfit for human habitation or is unfit in its current commercial, industrial or business use or is vacant and dilapidated, or whenever it otherwise appears to the public officer that any dwelling, building or structure is unfit for human habitation or is unfit for its current commercial, industrial or business use or is vacant or dilapidated, the public officer shall, if preliminary investigation discloses a basis for such charge, issue and cause to be served upon the owner and any parties in interest of such dwelling, building, or structure a complaint stating the charges in that respect and containing a notice that a hearing shall be held before the public officer. 618:
(a) The hearing pursuant to section 26-88 will be held at a place within the county as designated in the complaint on a day and time certain which shall not be less than ten nor more than 30 days after the service of this notice. The owner and any party in interest known to the public officer shall be given the right to file an answer to the complaint with the public officer and to appear in person or otherwise, to give testimony at the hearing at the place and time specified in the notice.
(b) The public officer shall preside at the hearing. The person conducting the hearing shall have authority to administer oaths or affirmations, examine witnesses, and receive evidence at the hearing. The rules of evidence prevailing in courts of law or equity shall not be controlling in the hearing. The proceedings at the hearing shall be recorded or taken down or made by such other procedure as may be undertaken either in verbatim or summary form so as to be reasonably accurate.

619:
(a) If, after the hearing, the public officer determines that the dwelling, building or structure under consideration is unfit for human habitation or is unfit for its current commercial, industrial or business use or is vacant and dilapidated, the public officer shall state in writing the findings of fact in support of such determination and shall issue and cause to be served upon the property owner an order which shall provide:
(1) A determination that the dwelling, building or structure can be repaired, improved or altered either at a cost of one-half or less of the value of the dwelling, building or structure exclusive of foundation and lot after the improvements have been made, or at a cost of more than one-half of the value of such structure exclusive of the foundation and lot after improvements have been made. If the cost to repair, improve or alter such structure is more than one-half of the value of such structure exclusive of foundation and lot after the improvements have been made, the order may find that such structure be vacated and removed or demolished within a specified time frame. If the dwelling, building or structure can be repaired, altered, or improved at a cost that is less than one-half of the value of such structure or structures exclusive of foundation and lot after improvements have been made, the order may find either that the structure be rendered fit for human habitation or current commercial, industrial or business use within a specified time or shall be vacated and closed and secured against entry.
(2) An enumeration of conditions which render the dwelling, building or structure unfit for human habitation or other uses and an enumeration of remedial action necessary to correct each of the conditions.
(3) That if the owner and/or parties in interest elect to undertake the necessary remedial action, the public officer shall establish:
a. A specific period of time, reasonably established in relationship to the remedial action, during which such action must be commenced, including, if necessary, separate commencement dates as to separate defects or work;
b. A specific period of time after the required commencement date of such remedial action, reasonably established in relationship to the necessary undertakings, within which such action shall be completed, including, if necessary, separate reasonable deadlines as to separate defects or work.
(4) That if the owner and/or the parties in interest do not notify the public officer of the intent to comply within 15 days of service of publication of the order for corrective action for a building, dwelling or structure which can be repaired at one-half or less of its value, the public officer shall subsequently commence and complete the vacating and closing of the dwelling, building or structure; or in case of a building or dwelling which cannot be repaired at one-half or less of the value, to commence and complete the vacating and removal or demolition of the building, dwelling or structure.
(5) A statement that failure to comply with the order within the required time set forth in this section is in violation of this article and shall subject the parties and property to the remedies of this article.
(b) Where a condition exists regarding any property which constitutes an immediate danger to persons or adjacent property, the public officer may shorten the time periods specified in this section.
(c) Prior to the effectuation of orders issued by the public officer pursuant to this section, the public officer shall submit such order to the governing authority of the county, and such order shall not be carried out without the written approval of the same.
(Code 1987, § 5-90; Ord. No. 2012-002, 3-15-2012)

625:
The county shall enforce the collection of any amount due on a lien arising under this article in the following manner:
(1) Amount. The amount of the lien shall be established as follows: There shall be an administrative fee assessed against all liened properties together with the costs of serving all notices required by this article. The amount of the lien shall also include the cost of vacating, removal, closing, repairing, or demolition which shall be the cost paid or incurred by the county in effecting action against any property. The administrative fee shall be in an amount as established by the board of commissioners from time to time.
(2) Notice of lien. In three equal annual payments, each of which shall become due and payable on the anniversary date of the initial payment made as prescribed in this section.
(3) Transfer of property. Should such property be sold, transferred or conveyed by the owner and/or parties in interest at any time prior to the termination of the three-year payment period, the entire balance due on such lien, with earned interest, shall be due and payable to the county.

This procedure shall be subject to the right of redemption by any person having any right, title or interest in or lien upon the property, all as provided by O.C.G.A. § 48-4-40.
(Code 1987, § 5-96; Ord. No. 2012-002, 3-15-2012)

742:
(a) The board of commissioners hereby adopts an internal grievance procedure providing for the resolution of complaints alleging any action prohibited by the office of revenue sharing's regulations implementing section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, as amended. Section 504 states, in part, that "no otherwise qualified handicapped individual shall, solely by reason of such person's handicap, be excluded from the participation in, be denied the benefits of, or be subjected to discrimination under any program or activity receiving financial assistance …. "
(b) Complaints should be addressed to the county.
(1) A complaint shall be filed in writing or verbally, contain the name and address of the person filing it, and briefly describe the alleged violation of the regulations.
(2) A complaint should be filed within ten days after the complainant becomes aware of the alleged violation.
(3) An investigation, if appropriate, shall follow a filing of a complaint. The investigation will be conducted by the handicap coordinator or such coordinator's designated appointee. These rules contemplate informal, but thorough, investigations, affording all interested persons and their representatives, if any, an opportunity to submit evidence relevant to a complaint. Under federal law, the board of commissioners need not process complaints from applicants for employment or from applicants for admission to postsecondary educational institutions.

(a) Public purpose. Based upon the reports of the U.S. Surgeon General and other reliable and credible scientific bodies indicating that the smoking of cigarettes, cigars, pipes and similar products, together with the secondary smoke generated thereby, is a contributing cause of illness among both smokers and passive smokers (those inhaling the smoke of other), to include, without limitation, cancer, heart disease and lung disorders; it is the finding of the board of commissioners of the county, that the smoke produced by the smoking of cigarettes, cigars, pipes and similar products is both hazardous and detrimental to the health, safety, well-being and comfort of the nonsmoking public. The Board of Commissioners of Liberty County, Georgia, therefore, finds that it is in the interest of public health, safety, and the general welfare of the employees, residents and visitors of the county to prohibit in county-owned or county-operated indoor facilities, parks and vehicles the inhaling, exhaling, burning, use, or carrying of any lighted or heated cigar, cigarette, or pipe, or any other lighted or heated tobacco product intended for inhalation, in any manner or in any form. The term "smoking" also includes the use of an e-cigarette that creates a vapor, in any manner or in any form, or the use of any oral smoking device for the purpose of circumventing the prohibition of smoking in this section.
(b) Definitions. As used in this section, the following words shall have the meanings as set forth below unless otherwise required by context:
Buildings and parks owned, operated or leased by the county includes those buildings, parks and other facilities, or parts thereof, under the control of the county.
E-cigarette means any electronic oral device, such as one composed of a heating element, battery and/or electronic circuit that provides a vapor of nicotine and/or other substances, and the use or inhalation of which simulates smoking. The term "e-cigarette" includes any such device, whether manufactured, distributed, marketeted, or sold as an e-cigarette, e-cigar or e-pipe, or under any other product name or descriptor and is considered smoking a tobacco-related product.
Smoking means the inhaling, exhaling, burning or carrying any lighted or heated cigar, cigarette, or pipe, or any other lighted or heated tobacco product intended for inhalation, in any manner or in any form. The term "smoking" also includes the use of an e-cigarette that creates a vapor, in any manner or in any form, or the use of any oral smoking device for the purpose of circumventing the prohibition of smoking in this section.
Tobacco-related products means any product from the plant called tobacco or the family of plants from the genus Nicotiana. These products shall include, but are not limited to, pipe tobacco, smoking tobacco, cigars, cigarettes, cigarillos, chewing tobacco, snuff or smokeless tobacco.
(c) Tobacco-related product use prohibited.
(1) Tobacco-related products are prohibited in and throughout all buildings and parks owned, operated or leased by the county, as well as prohibited within 25 feet of the exterior of such buildings on property owned, operated, or leased by the county.
(2) Tobacco-related product use is likewise prohibited in all enclosed-cab vehicles owned and/or operated by the county, unless the individual wishing to use a tobacco-related product first receives the express consent of all other occupants of the vehicle.
(d) Notice. The county administrator, or his designee, shall cause signs to be conspicuously posted throughout buildings and parks owned, operated or leased by the county informing the public that using a tobacco-related product is prohibited by county ordinance. The size, design, location and content of such signs shall be determined by the county administrator, or his designee.
(e) Penalty. Any person found violating the provisions of this section, upon conviction, shall be fined not less than $50.00, but no more than $100.00, per offense.
(f) Enforcement. The magistrate court of the county shall have jurisdiction over violations of this section and all procedures for enforcement hereof shall be as provided in O.C.G.A. Title 15, Chapter 10, Article 4 (O.C.G.A. § 15-10-60 et seq.), as amended. Complaints of violations of any provision contained herein shall be brought before the magistrate court on a citation issued by the county administrator or his designee or the chief magistrate of the county and shall be prosecuted through that court. Violations of this section will be tried upon citations either with or without a prosecuting attorney as determined by the said county administrator (or his designee). Service of citation shall be performed by the constable of the magistrate court of the county. Citations shall meet all the official requirements as specified in the O.C.G.A. § 15-10-63, as amended.

(a) Fee established. To discourage excessive false alarms at any residential, commercial, industrial, institutional, educational or other location and better protect the lives and property of the citizens and residents of the county, as well as to reduce unnecessary use of public safety resources and help to defray the costs of responding to false alarms, a false alarm service fee is hereby established.

The owner or lessee of any residential, commercial, industrial, institutional, educational or other property with an alarm system shall pay to the board of commissioners a false alarm service fee for each false alarm responded to by public safety personnel, based upon the total number of false alarms occurring at such location during the preceding 12 months. Number of False Alarms Within a 12-Month Period | Fee
1—4 | No charge
5—10 | $100.00
11—20 | $150.00
21—30 | $200.00
31 or more | $300.00
All false alarm service fees assessed by this section shall be due and payable within 30 days following notice thereof.

Following a false alarm at any residential, commercial, industrial, institutional, educational or other property, the false alarm administrator shall notify the responsible owner or lessee of the alarm system and the false alarm service fee due under this section. (1) Member professional backgrounds. At all times, the governing board shall endeavor to appoint to the commission at least one member who has a professional background in the field of real estate development, at least one member who has a professional background in the field of building and construction, at least one member who has a professional background in business management, at least one member who has a professional background in general industry or industrial management, at least one member who has a professional background in the field of natural resources or environmental protection; provided that the governing board is not strictly obligated to appoint members from the aforementioned fields, but shall in all instances appoint members it determines to be the most qualified and appropriate, taking into consideration the desirability of having members from the various fields enumerated in this subsection. a. Temporary vacancy on the board; or
b. Refusal of any member due to a conflict of interest as determined by such member.

Approved container/receptacle means a galvanized metal or durable plastic container of a capacity not less than 20 gallons and not to exceed 32 gallons, having two handles on the side thereof or a bail by which it may be lifted, with a tight-fitting metal or plastic top with a handle and so constructed as to permit the free discharge of its contents. Containers shall be waterproof. Oil or grease drums, paint cans and similar salvaged containers shall not be acceptable.
Asbestos means any naturally occurring hydrated mineral silicates separable into commercially used fibers, specifically the asbestiform varieties of serpentine, chrysotile, cummingtomitegrunerite, amosite, reiheckite, crocidolite, anthophyllite, tremolite, and actinolite.
Biomedical waste means pathological waste, biological waste, cultures and stocks of infectious agents and associated biologicals, contaminated animal carcasses (body parts, their bedding, and other wastes from such animals), sharps, chemotherapy waste, discarded medical equipment and parts, not including expendable supplies and materials which have not been contaminated, as further defined in rule 391-3-4-.15 (Ga. Walls | 12 gauge

| 10 gauge for all over 4 cu. yd.

Doors | 14 gauge
Commercial establishment means any hotel, motel, trailer/mobile home parks, apartment house, rooming house, rental property of two or more multiple-dwelling units, business, retail stores, industrial, public or semipublic establishment of any nature or kind whatsoever other than a single dwelling unit/residential unit and condominiums.
Commercial/industrial refuse means waste material from industrial processes, manufacturing, canneries, slaughterhouses, packing plants, poultry processing or similar industries, and large quantities of condemned foods. The term "commercial refuse" also includes waste material from the construction, remodeling and repair operations on houses, commercial buildings, multiple-dwellings and other structures and includes such materials as concrete, bricks, plaster, stone, earth, lumber, roofing materials, gutters, shavings and sawdust.
Compactor container means a manufactured commercial container of a specified size with a self-contained compacting mechanism or an external compactor which is designed to be used in conjunction with the disposal/collection system.
Composting means the controlled biological decomposition of organic waste.
Condominium means individual ownership units in a multifamily structure with a front and back entrance to each unit on the ground level.
Construction/demolition waste means the waste building materials and rubble resulting from construction, remodeling, repair, and demolition operations associated with such things as pavements, houses, commercial buildings and other structures. Such wastes include, but are not limited to wood, bricks, metal, concrete, wallboard, paper or cardboard.
Convenience center means a county disposal site where county residents deposit refuse by type (i.e., household, yard, white goods and furniture, and recyclables) for collection and disposal/processing by the county sanitation department.
Department means the county sanitation department.
Disposal facility means any facility or location where any treatment, utilization, processing or disposition of solid waste occurs as licensed/permitted by the state through the department of natural resources.
Disposal operation means the performance of solid waste disposal, which includes administration, personnel, land, equipment, design, and other elements necessary or used in the work of solid waste disposal.
Disposal site means the location where the final disposition of solid waste occurs.
Division means the environmental protection division of the Georgia Department of Natural Resources.
Garbage means food waste, including waste accumulations of animal or vegetable matter used or intended for use as food or that attends the preparation, use, cooking, dealing in or storing of meat, fish, fowl, fruit or vegetables.
Hazardous waste means any solid waste which has been defined as a hazardous waste in regulations promulgated by the board of natural resources for the state.

Industrial waste means solid waste generated by manufacturing or industrial processes that is not a hazardous waste as defined herein.

Leachate means a liquid that has passed through or emerged from solid waste and contains soluble, suspended, or miscible materials removed from such wastes.

Litter means all garbage, refuse, waste materials, sand, gravel, slag, brickbats, rubbish, tin cans, trash, debris, dead animals, or any other discarded substance which is not handled in accordance with the provisions of this chapter.
Medical waste means all biomedical waste as defined in this section.

Owner means any person owning, leasing, renting, occupying or managing any premises in the jurisdiction of the board of county commissioners.
Person means the State of Georgia or any other state or any agency or institution thereof, and any municipality, political subdivision, public or private corporation, special district empowered to engage in solid waste management activities, individual, partnership, association or other entity in Georgia or any other state. Recyclable means any waste stream product which can be reclaimed and reprocessed by others into its original or modified form for reuse.

Recycling container means a specifically designated container, normally identified with the recycling logo into which recyclable products are placed as specifically designated on the container.
Refuse means garbage, rubbish or commercial refuse.
Residential unit means any freestanding structure or shelter or any part thereof used or constructed for use as a residence for one family.
Rubbish means wastepaper, cartons, boxes, wood, tree branches, yard trimmings, furniture, appliances, metals, cans, glass, crockery, dunnage, and/or similar materials.
Sanitary landfill means a disposal site where putrescible solid wastes are disposed of by means of placing an earth cover thereon, as permitted by the state through the environmental protection division.
Sanitary landfilling means an engineered method of disposing of putrescible solid wastes on land by spreading the waste in thin layers, compacting the waste to the smallest practical volume, placing an earth cover thereon and such other measures as are necessary to protect human health and the environment.
Scavenge means the uncontrolled picking from discarded solid waste materials.
Scavenger, private contractor, or commercial sanitation firm means any person other than a municipality, who is licensed by the county to collect, remove, salvage or dispose of refuse from one or more public or private premises, other than the person's own, whether or not under written contract, and whether or not for compensation.
Solid waste means putrescible and nonputrescible wastes, except water-carried body waste and materials destined for recycling, and shall include garbage, rubbish (paper, cartons, boxes, wood, tree branches, yard trimmings, furniture, and appliances, metal, tin cans, glass, crockery, or dunnage), ashes, street refuse, dead animals, sewage sludges, animal manures, industrial wastes (waste materials generated from industrial operations) residue from incineration, food processing wastes, demolition wastes, and other waste material in solid or semi-solid state not otherwise defined in this chapter or by the state.
Solid waste enterprise fund means a self-sufficient, revenue-producing fund and full cost accounting system which encompasses the total cost of solid waste disposal operations of the county as managed by the board of commissioners, thereby preventing subsidizing the cost of solid waste disposal operations from the county's general fund.
Solid waste handling means the storage, collection, transportation, treatment, utilization, processing, or disposal of solid waste, or any combination thereof.
Solid waste handling facility means any location where any storage, collection, transportation, treatment, utilization, processing or disposal of solid waste or any combination thereof occurs.
Solid waste handling permit means written authorization granted to a person by the director, EPD, DNR, of the State of Georgia to engage in solid waste handling.
Solid Waste Management Act or the Act refers to O.C.G.A. § 12-8-20.
Solid waste task force means a board of persons appointed by the board of commissioners to oversee the solid waste management operations of the county. 802:
The county will operate appropriate convenience centers approved by the board of commissioners. Normally, a convenience center will provide bulk collection containers for household solid waste (putrescible); recyclables; yard waste on a specified scheduled basis; and large household items such as furniture and appliances on a specified scheduled basis. Each convenience center will have posted the hours of operation. (a) All commercial establishments, condominiums, and townhouses within the county shall be required to provide for commercial collection/disposal of all solid waste, except for recyclables, when no recycling container is provided at such locations. The county will not collect refuse from commercial establishments or multiple-dwelling units unless it is placed in commercial containers, properly located. Uncontaminated cardboard boxes shall be cleaned of all noncardboard/paper packing materials, flattened and placed in available cardboard recycling containers. It shall be unlawful for any commercial establishment to dispose of refuse in green boxes marked for residential refuse only.
(d) Where the occupants of two or more commercial establishments share the use of a refuse container, it shall be the joint responsibility of the users to maintain the area surrounding such container clean and free of accumulations of refuse.

(f) All garbage and rubbish generated at commercial or residential commercial establishments shall be free of liquid and placed in watertight paper or plastic bags with tops secured prior to placement in commercial containers.
(g) A handling fee will be charged on any commercial containers containing any of the following items:
(1) Large household or industrial appliances.
(2) Furniture.
(3) Tires.
(4) Wooden crates.
(5) Logs or limbs over four feet in length or four inches in diameter.
(6) Bed springs.
(7) Rock, dirt, concrete blocks, etc.
(8) Uncontainable garbage, yard debris, and household trash.
(9) Asbestos or asbestos-containing materials.
(10) Any liquid in excess of one U.S. gallon.

f. (a) Transfer station. This facility accepts conforming nonhazardous solid waste from collection sources such as jurisdictional municipal solid waste collection services (public and privately owned), county-operated solid waste collection services (rural and commercial clients), jurisdictional commercial and business (contract and cash) customers and nonjurisdictional private residential and nonjurisdictional commercial and business clients. All solid waste processed into the transfer station is charged a published disposal fee based on the customer and the solid waste material. Disposal fees are established by the county board of commissioners (see section 34-71) and are periodically adjusted. The current fee schedule is available through the county solid waste, at the transfer station.
(b) Convenience centers. These facilities, located throughout the unincorporated area of the county, provide interim solid waste disposal/collection points for the unincorporated residents and municipal residents of Allenhurst, Flemington, Gumbranch, Midway, Riceboro and Walthourville. (This excludes Hinesville residents who have full range solid waste collection provided by the city and thus are not assessed for associated operational/disposal costs.) These convenience centers are for use by single-family residential property owners of the unincorporated area and municipalities described above. Operational costs for these facilities are recouped through the county solid waste assessment. Use by unauthorized commercial and business or nonjurisdictional parties is prohibited. Typically, each center includes one household waste compactor with a 38- to 40-cubic-yard enclosed receiving container and two 40-cubic-yard open top containers for disposal of yard waste, scrap metal and appliances (white goods) and bulky waste (brown goods). Additionally, each center provides facilities for acceptance of recyclable items. Service fees (annual residential solid waste assessment) for authorized customers are established by the county board of commissioners (see section 34-71) and are periodically adjusted. A listing of these fees is available, through the county solid waste authority, at the commissioner's office or at the county solid waste authority transfer station.
(c) Rural dumpster sites. The county operates several rural dumpster sites in the unincorporated area of the county. Until these sites are closed, their use is restricted to those jurisdictional residents who pay for their operation through the annual residential solid waste assessment. Use by non-jurisdictional parties and/or commercial or business enterprises is strictly prohibited.
(d) Recycling facilities. Six additional recycling facilities are located in the municipal boundaries of Hinesville (four locations), Walthourville (one facility) and Riceboro (one facility). These facilities, in addition to those co-located at each convenience center, are operated by the county solid waste for the sole use of county residents. No business or commercial use is authorized. The disposal of any type of nonconforming waste is unauthorized at these facilities. Recyclable items are to be placed in the appropriate bins or containers. Operational costs of these facilities are recouped through the annual residential solid waste assessment.
(Code 1987, § 15-202; Ord. No. 2006-001, 2-1-2006; Ord. No. 2019-003, 7-18-2019)

822:
(a) Generally. The cost to operate the county convenience centers, rural dumpster sites and recycling facilities is funded by the annual residential solid waste assessment. Use of these facilities is strictly reserved for residents of the county who pay for their operation through the annual assessment. Unauthorized users will be cited and include those who plan to use (are physically located at a site) or have used a facility to discard solid waste or recyclables and persons who are scavenging or have scavenged items from the solid waste collection containers or recycling facilities. Unauthorized users will be cited and will be subject to court fees, fines and disposal costs as determined by the county magistrate court, the table of offenses, fines and disposal charges (see section 34-105) and the county solid waste.
(b) Proof of authorization. The prima facie evidence of unauthorized use is the user's vehicle license plate. Out-of-county plates suggest the user is unauthorized. However, the out-of-county user is authorized to use the facility if they have received and paid the current annual residential solid waste assessment. A current paid receipt for the solid waste assessment supported by a second form of personal identification validates the authorized facility use by such residents. Officers of the county charged with validating solid waste facility users are to explain the reasons for verifying the user's residency; advise the out-of-county user to carry a copy of the paid solid waste assessment receipt; take the users name, home address and telephone number and license plate number and allow use of the facility. The name, address, license plate number and phone number will be transmitted to the litter control deputy for validation of authorized use. Fraudulent cases will be cited for unauthorized use through magistrate court.
(c) Identification. Unauthorized users will be identified as follows:
(1) Observation by the county litter control deputy or other solid waste employee. Observed use includes the physical act of waste disposal or being at a site with the intent to use the facility for waste disposal; or being on site to scavenge; being found in the act of scavenging; or found with scavenged material in their possession.
(2) Reporting of apparent unauthorized use by the general public under the silent witness program or by calling the offices of the county commission or the solid waste authority. In such cases, prima facie evidence is being on site using a vehicle with an out-of-county license plate or operation of a vehicle with affixed business logo operated by the potential offender who has or plans to dispose of waste typical of the business, and, if available, a description of the individual and the vehicle, the time and facility being used, and the type of waste being disposed of or scavenged. Additional evidence of unauthorized use is identifiable discards of solid waste (letters, bank receipts, credit card slips, magazines with address labels, shipping containers with ship-to addresses, business papers, etc.). Reports of this type will be accepted telephonically, in writing or verbally.
(3) Apprehension by an officer of the law. In this case, the apprehending officer will issue a citation to the offending party. No warnings will be given.
(4) After-the-fact clean-up of materials disposed of at any of the county facilities or materials discarded elsewhere in the county (private or publicly owned lands). In such cases, prima facie evidence will be any item recovered from the discards which bears a name, address or other form of personal identification which would indicate the last ownership of the improperly discarded items.
(d) Citation. Citations for unauthorized use of a county solid waste collection/disposal/recycling facility, unless issued by an officer of the law other than the county litter control deputy, will be written by the county litter control deputy and prosecuted through the county magistrate court. No warning will be issued since all facilities have been signed advising that unauthorized use is prohibited.
(e) Payment of fines and disposal charges. The county magistrate court will prosecute each case. The county solid waste authority will provide the court with calculated weight tickets detailing the associated pull fees, disposal charges and clean-up costs as appropriate for each citation. These costs are to be added to the fines presented in the tables of offenses, fines and disposal charges shown below. Upon payment to the court, the applicable fines and disposal charges will to turned over to the county solid waste through the office of the Clerk of the Superior Court.
(Code 1987, § 15-203; Ord. No. 2006-001, 2-1-2006; Ord. No. 2019-003, 7-18-2019)

(a) Upon receipt of a petition in the form and format as specified by the board of commissioners seeking a change of name of an existing named road, the board of commissioners shall take under consideration, but be under no compulsion to grant, said request; provided that any such petition shall contain the signatures of the owners or their authorized representatives (as specified below) of not less than 60 percent of the parcels of property abutting said public road. At its discretion, the board of commissioners may, but shall not be required, to hold a public hearing prior to deciding the issue of the proposed name change.
(b) For purposes of this section, the owner of the abutting property shall be deemed to be the person or entity returning the property for ad valorem taxes in the office of the county tax commissioner.

(1) The name of said roadway has been changed within the previous 120 months; or
(2) If a petition to change the name of said roadway has been denied by the board of commissioners within the previous 120 months.

837:
This article is intended to require notice of timber harvesting operations within the unincorporated areas of Liberty County pursuant to O.C.G.A. §12-6-24, and, in accordance with Title 32 of the Official Code of Georgia, provide regulations further governing use of public roads by persons engaged in said timber harvesting operations in order to assure the public safety and to protect the county roadways and environment.
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
838:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
County administrator means the county administrator for Liberty County, or his or her designee.
Notice means the notice required to be given to the public works department by the timber harvester as provided herein.
Person means any natural person, firm, corporation, limited liability company, partnership, or other legal entity of whatever form.
Public works department means the Liberty County Public Works Department.
Public works director means the Director of the Liberty County Public Works Department.
Surety bond means a valid surety bond, executed by a surety corporation authorized to transact business in the State of Georgia, protecting the County against any damage caused by such person or firm in an amount specified by the governing authority of Liberty County not exceeding $5,000.00 or, at the option of the timber harvester, a valid irrevocable letter of credit issued by a bank or savings and loan association, as defined in O.C.G.A. § 7-1-4, in the amount of an in lieu of such bond. Any such surety bond or letter of credit shall be in form prescribed by or acceptable to the county administrator and shall be for the calendar year in which delivered; provided that no more than one bond or letter of credit shall be required from each timber harvester, regardless of the number of tracts harvested in the county for so long as the bond or letter of credit remains in effect. The bond or letter of credit required herein shall be valid only for the calendar year in which it was delivered.
Timber means softwood or hardwood trees harvested for commercial purposes.
Timber harvester means any person harvesting standing timber in any unincorporated area of Liberty County, Georgia for delivery as pulpwood, logs, poles, posts, or wood chips to any woodyard or processing plant located inside or outside the State of Georgia.
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
839:
(a) Written notice shall be required of any timber harvester harvesting timber in the unincorporated areas of the County for each separate tract to be harvested. Said written notice shall be (a) delivered to the public works department prior to entering onto the subject tract, if possible, but in no event later than 24 hours after entering onto said tract; and (b) in such form and containing such information as set forth in O.C.G.A. § 12-6-24(b)(1). Notice shall be effective only as to the tract described therein upon receipt by the public works department (as confirmed by written acknowledgment from said public works department to the timber harvester) and compliance with all other applicable requirements of this article. Further, within 24 hours following completion of timber harvesting operations, the responsible timber harvester shall give notice of cessation of cutting to the public works director or other designee of the county administrator. Such notice may be given in person, by transmission of an electronic record via telefacsimile, e-mail, or such other means as approved by the governing authority of the county, or by mail.
(b) Upon notification published by the Director of the Georgia Forestry Commission that a state-wide notification website or platform is available for public use, persons wishing to utilize said website or platform to provide the notice required by this article may do so at their option, and the county will accept notifications submitted in this manner. On and after a date specified and published by the Director of the Georgia Forestry Commission, use of the aforesaid state-wide notification website or platform shall be mandatory and shall be the sole means of providing the notice required by this article. On and after said date, submission of the notice by any of the means listed in this section shall cease and will no longer be deemed acceptable or in compliance with this article.
(c) At all times during any timber harvesting operations subject to this article, the timber harvester shall additionally ensure that the requisite notice is continuously posted and displayed in good condition and in a conspicuous location on each tract of land identified in said notice. For purposes of this section, the notice shall be deemed posted in a "conspicuous location" if clearly visible and located in the immediate vicinity where the entrance road or trail providing vehicular access to the subject tract meets the nearest public right-of-way.
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
840:
(a) A surety bond shall not be required prior to notice becoming effective. However, following the giving of any notice, in the event that the public works director determines that any activities relating to the timber harvesting are being conducted in a manner that poses likelihood of damage to any public rights-of-way or danger to the public safety, the public works department shall be authorized to demand a surety bond from the timber harvester. The surety bond shall be delivered to the public works department within three business days following receipt of written demand for the same, unless within said time a written notice of appeal is received by the public works department contesting the requirement of the surety bond. In the event of such contest, the public works department shall, no later than five business days, schedule an administrative hearing in such matter before the county administrator, who shall deliver a decision within three business days of said hearing. The decision of the county administrator shall be conclusive and binding for all purposes. Following any contest as provided above, all timber harvesting authorized pursuant to the applicable notice shall be suspended until the surety bond, if any, is delivered to the public works department as required by the county administrator.
(b) The bond or letter of credit required by this section shall protect the county against any damage requiring re-ditching or repair of existing ditch structures or the removal of any harvesting residue, including tree tops, debris, logs, pulpwood and other materials, placed in or around the county's rights-of-way caused by such person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit. The proceeds of such bond or letter of credit shall be available to reimburse the county for any cost incurred to repair such damages or remove such debris in or around the county's rights-of-way. The proceeds of such bond or letter of credit shall also be available to reimburse the county for any costs incurred to maintain or repair county roads damaged by the ingress or egress of motor vehicles engaged in the harvest operations located within 500 feet of any point of ingress or egress of the timber harvesting operation.
(c) In the event a bond or letter of credit tendered pursuant to the requirements of this article is revoked by the surety or bank, then a valid replacement bond or letter of credit must be delivered by the timber harvester to the public works department within five business days after the date of revocation in order for timber harvesting operations to continue. In addition, if the timber harvester caused its revocation, the amount of the bond or letter of credit required shall be increased to $7,500.00 after the first revocation, and $10,000.00 after a second revocation caused by the person or firm tendering the bond or letter of credit. The maximum amount of the bond or letter of credit shall not exceed $10,000.00.
(d) In no event shall the delivery of a surety bond (or the failure to require a surety bond) limit the liability of any person engaged in timber harvesting and related activities for damages to public property or rights-of-way or for other personal injury or property damage, and all such persons shall be and remain at all times fully liable to the county for any and all such injury and damage. Furthermore, the right of the county to call such bond or letter of credit in accordance with the provisions of this article shall be in addition to any other remedies available to the county at law or in equity for damage to county roads or rights-of-way.
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
841:
(a) When damage results from a timber harvester's activities, the public works director or such other designee of the county administrator shall make and provide a written claim to the timber harvester causing the damage within 30 business days after the public works director becomes aware of the damage. Such claim may be given in person, by telefacsimile, email or mail. The claim shall describe the damage in detail and, in compliance with subsection (b) immediately below, give the timber harvester the opportunity to repair such damage within 30 days of the notification; provided, however, the county shall be authorized to repair the damage immediately if the public works director or other designee of the county administrator determines that the conditions present a threat to public safety, health or welfare and, upon making such repairs, shall present to the timber harvester and the issuer of the applicable bond or letter of credit an itemized list of expenses incurred as a claim against the timber harvester and the issuer of its bond or letter of credit. Upon the issuance of a claim as provided in this section the public works director or other designee of the county administrator shall notify the issuer of the bond or letter of credit that a claim has been made and will be resolved or adjudicated according to the terms of this article.
(b) Within 30 days of receipt of the written claim described in subsection (a) immediately above, the timber harvester against whom the claim is submitted may:
(1) Repair such damage at his or its own expense with the approval and supervision of the public works director or other designee of the county administrator. When repairs are completed to the satisfaction of the public works director or other designee of the county administrator, the public works director or other designee of the county administrator shall provide a written notification of satisfactory completion within five business days to the timber harvester and to the surety issuing the bond or the bank issuing the letter of credit, thereby terminating the claim.
(2) In the event of inclement weather or other factors preventing repair of the damage, request a 30 day extension to repair the damage from the public works director or other designee of the county administrator who provided written notice of the claim, provided that no extensions shall exceed 90 days from the date the claim was tendered. Approval of any extension shall be at the discretion of the public works director or other designee of the county administrator.
(3) Appeal the claim to the Magistrate Court of Liberty County. Any such appeal must name the issuer of the bond or letter of credit as a party, who shall be served with all pleadings in the action and shall have the right to appear. The magistrate court will hear evidence and arguments within 30 days of the written appeal and issue a ruling within ten days of such hearing. Any such appeal shall toll the 30-day period, or any extension thereof, required by subsection (b)(2) above. If the magistrate court rules in favor of the timber harvester against whom the claim was made, the county shall have no right to recover any proceeds of the bond or letter of credit, and judgment shall be entered against the county. If the magistrate court rules in favor of the county, the court shall determine the amount of damages to which the county is entitled to recover and enter judgment accordingly; the county shall be authorized to call the bond or letter of credit and recover from the proceeds thereof an amount equal to the judgment entered by the court, up to the total amount of the bond or letter of credit. The portion of any judgment entered in favor of the county that exceeds the amount of the bond or letter of credit shall be subject to collection by any additional remedies at law or equity.
(c) In the event the timber harvester against whom the claim has been submitted fails to take any of the actions allowed under subsection (b) above within the time required therein, said timber harvester shall be deemed to have waived any and all rights to contest the call of the bond or letter of credit.
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
842:
Prior to commencing timber harvesting operations, the public works director shall inspect the point of access to the public road from the tract described in the notice in order to determine its suitability. If a culvert is required at the point of access, it shall be promptly installed by the timber harvester as directed by the public works director. In the event that a timber harvester elects to commence operations prior to inspection by the public works director (and prior to the installation of any needed culvert), the timber harvester shall deliver the surety bond required by this article prior to commencing timber harvesting operations, in which case notice shall not be or remain effective for such timber harvesting operations until delivery of said surety bond as required by this article.
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
843:
Prior to commencing any timber harvesting operations, the timber harvester shall post two signs in each direction from the point of access onto the involved public road. One sign at a distance of 1,000 feet from the point of access stating "Warning: Logging Operations Ahead," and one sign at a distance of 500 feet stating "Slow Truck Entering Highway." All signs shall be 36 inches × 36 inches, erected in a diamond shape, painted orange with black legend and posted at least three feet from the travel surface of the roadway. Prior to and at all times during any timber harvesting operations subject to this article, the timber harvester shall additionally ensure that the requisite notice is continuously posted and displayed in good condition and in a conspicuous location on each tract of land identified in said notice. For purposes of this Section, the notice shall be deemed posted in a "conspicuous location" if clearly visible and located in the immediate vicinity where the entrance road or trail providing vehicular access to the subject tract meets the nearest public right-of-way.
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
844:
During the period of timber harvesting operations, the timber harvester shall comply with the following:
(1) All harvesting operations shall be conducted on the tract identified in the notice and off public roads and rights-of-way. Logging and skidding of logs on public roads and rights-of-way are strictly prohibited.
(2) Ditches constituting a part of the public drainage system or otherwise benefitting a public right-of-way shall be kept clear of all debris and residue at all times to permit proper drainage.
(3) There shall be no blockage of public roads or rights-of-way at the access site, and all public roads and rights-of-way must remain open and kept free of debris and residue at all times.
(4) No equipment, trucks, trailers, or other personal property shall be parked or located on any public road or right-of-way.
(5) Mud shall not be carried onto paved public roads by logging vehicles. Where necessary, a temporary construction exit of gravel shall be maintained by the timber harvester to eliminate any hazard to traffic or unsightly conditions on the public right-of-way.
(6) During periods of rain or inclement weather, logging vehicles shall not be operated over the unimproved public roads when such travel causes sufficient damage to the road system that the passage of smaller and lighter vehicles is hampered.
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
845:
(a) Upon notice from the public works director or other designee of the county administrator, work on any project that is being done contrary to the provisions of this article shall be immediately stopped. Such notice shall be in writing and shall be given to the timber harvester and the owner of the subject property, and shall state the conditions under which work may resume. When an emergency exists, written notice shall not be required.
(b) If the conditions are not brought into compliance within five business days of the notice, the public works department shall be authorized to accomplish the work (with costs thereof to be reimbursed by the timber harvester), and any violation of the provisions of this article shall be punished as for a misdemeanor.
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
846:
Consistent with O.C.G.A. § 12-6-24:
(a) No fee shall be charged to provide and submit the notice required by this article,
(b) No permit, including a driveway permit, shall be required of the person or firm engaged in a timber harvesting operation as defined by said Code section; provided that timber harvesters may be asked to consult with the public works department for the purpose of minimizing damage to the county's roads, rights-of-way and infrastructure, and are urged to follow recommendations from county officials. In the event that a timber harvester elects not to follow any recommendation made by the public works department, the timber harvester shall deliver the surety bond required by this article prior to commencing timber harvesting operations, in which case notice shall not be or remain effective for such timber harvesting operations until delivery of said surety bond as required by this article. Notwithstanding the forgoing, timber harvesters bear ultimate responsibility for their actions, and nothing in this article shall preclude the county from taking any and all legal action necessary to protect its property and the health, safety and welfare of its citizens.
(c) This article applies to activities which qualify as forestry land management practices or agricultural operations under O.C.G.A. § 12-7-17 (5) and (6) on land that is zoned for or used for forestry, silvicultural or agricultural purposes. It shall not authorize land disturbing activities incidental to development in conflict with the limitations set forth in O.C.G.A. § 12-7-17(6).
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)
847:
(a) Any person violating any of the provisions of this article shall be guilty of a misdemeanor prosecutable in the Magistrate Court of Liberty County and punishable by a fine not to exceed $500.00 for each violation and imprisonment in the county jail for a period of not longer than 12 months; provided that violation of the notice requirements of this article shall be punishable by a fine not exceeding $1,500.00.
(b) The public works director or other designee of the county administrator shall be authorized to issue citations in order to initiate such prosecution.
(c) The imposition of any fine or other sentence pursuant to this section shall in no way limit the liability of any person for damage done to public property or public rights-of-way, and the county shall be authorized to additionally pursue recovery for any such damage by any and all means permitted by law or in equity, to include, without limitation, the filing of a suit for damages, or the seeking of injunctive relief to stop any such damage.
(Ord. No. 2021-003, § I, 6-17-2021)

851:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
County administrator means the individual designated by the board of commissioners as [the] county administrator responsible for the general supervision of all county departments, including the county water system.
Customer means every person who is responsible for contracting (expressly or implicitly) with the county in obtaining, having or using water through the water system. The term "customer" shall also include illicit users of the water or water system.
Department director or director means the person designated by the county as director of the county water system.
Easement means any acquired legal right for the specific use of land owned by others.
Grant means any federal or state grant or loan made to the county in connection with the water system, and any bonds issued or other documents executed in connection therewith, and all requirements and conditions imposed upon the county by virtue of the same.
Ordinance means this ordinance, consisting of articles I through IV, as the same may hereafter be supplemented, amended, expanded, or otherwise modified.
User means any person who receives water from the county water system.
Water system or county water system means those tanks, wells, structures, valves, meter boxes, backflow prevention devices, facilities, lines, pipes, equipment, and other improvements owned, in whole or in part, or operated by the county and used in the withdrawal, pumping, storage, testing, treatment, processing, distribution, and delivery of potable water to the public, as said water system presently exists or as it may hereafter be improved, expanded or modified.
(Code 1987, § 13-1; Ord. No. 2013-007, § I, 12-3-2013)
852:
(a) Generally. This chapter regulates the connection to and use of the county water system.
(b) Administration. Except as otherwise provided in this chapter or directed by the county administrator, the department director or his agent shall administer, implement and enforce the provisions of the chapter.
(Code 1987, § 13-2; Ord. No. 2013-007, § I, 12-3-2013)
853:
(a) No person shall make a connection to or obtain water services from the county water system without first obtaining a permit for the same from the department director or his designee as required by this chapter.
(b) Subject to those exceptions and limitations set forth in O.C.G.A. § 36-60-17.1 and any other applicable state or federal law, the water distribution system of any building constructed after January 1, 2014, in which plumbing fixtures are installed shall be connected to the county water system, if water service from said system is available. Water service shall be deemed available if water service from the county water system is furnished within 200 feet of said building and that the provision of water services thereto is otherwise feasible, as determined by the county administrator; provided, however, that in no event shall this section obligate the county to expand the water system or otherwise extend service to any property not then currently served. Any expansion of the water system or other provision of water therefrom shall be undertaken at the sole and complete discretion of the county.
(c) Customers shall receive water services exclusively from the water system and no other source without the written consent of the county administrator, except that private wells located on or serving the customer's property may be used for irrigation purposes (and for irrigation purposes only).
(Code 1987, § 13-3; Ord. No. 2013-007, § I, 12-3-2013)
854:
(a) The owner of the land upon which a water connection is desired, or the owner's authorized agent, shall make application on a form furnished by the county. The permit application shall be supplemented by the owner's drawings, plans, specifications or other such information which, in the judgment of the department director, is considered to be pertinent to the desired connection.
(b) All costs and expenses incidental to connection to the water system shall be borne by the owner. The owner shall indemnify the county against any loss or damage to the county water system that may be directly or indirectly occasioned by the connection.
(c) It shall be a violation of this chapter for any user to knowingly make any false statements, representations or certifications in any application, record, report, plan or other documentation filed, or required to be maintained, pursuant to this chapter.
(Code 1987, § 13-4; Ord. No. 2013-007, § I, 12-3-2013)
856:
(a) The consumption of all water furnished by the county water system shall be measured by water meters approved by the department director; provided that the department director shall not issue a connection permit or authorize the installation of a water meter until the fees required by this chapter for such connection and metering have been paid. All water meters and related shutoff valves shall be and remain the property of the county.
(b) The department director shall be authorized to make a determination of the number of meters that may be required for condominiums, apartment buildings, apartment complexes or townhouses, shopping centers, mobile home parks, and other multifamily and multi-unit properties; provided, however, that sub-metering for all such properties shall be required to the extent practicable, as determined by the department director, and as may otherwise be mandated by applicable law. The owner of any such multifamily or multi-unit property shall submit plans, drawings, surveys, and other information as requested by the department director to assist the department director in making his determination under this section.
(c) All connections to the county water system shall be made, and all water meters shall be installed, at such location as may be determined by the department director or his designee. Without limiting the foregoing, and absent the written authorization of the department director:
(1) All water meters shall be installed at an easily accessible location on or near the property line of the premises being served adjacent to the public right-of-way; and
(2) Water meters shall not be installed behind enclosed fences, in paved driveways or in paved parking areas.
(d) The size, materials of construction, and methods of construction of all pipes, lines, and other facilities connecting to the county water system shall conform to all applicable local, state, and federal chapters, statutes, regulations, codes, and laws, including, without limitation, all plumbing, building, environmental, safety, health, and technical codes.
(Code 1987, § 13-5.1; Ord. No. 2013-007, § I, 12-3-2013)
857:
Any construction work relating to the county water system and conducted on the public right-of-way or any public property by anyone other than county personnel shall be conducted only with proper, written permission from the department director. All disturbed areas as a result of such construction shall be restored, at the sole cost of the person undertaking the work, to substantially the same condition as prior to the disturbance. The scheduling of such construction activities shall be as approved by the department director if such scheduling approval is determined to be in the public's best interest. Additionally, as a condition to any such construction work, the director shall be authorized to require such deposit, bond, indemnification, and other assurances as the director determines appropriate.
(Code 1987, § 13-6; Ord. No. 2013-007, § I, 12-3-2013)
858:
(a) Permanent easements granted, obtained, or otherwise used by the county in connection with the water system are established so that inter alia the county may properly install, inspect, observe, measure, sample, repair, protect, maintain, replace, and operate said water system. It is essential that access to the easement not be obstructed. Although the property owner owns the underlying fee simple title to the land within the easement area subject to the easement rights, all construction, digging, grubbing, clearing, filling, or other earth moving or construction activities by the owner in the permanent easement area are prohibited without prior permission from the department director or his designee. Permanent structures shall not be permitted within the easement or easement setback as provided in subsection (b) of this section. In addition, upon demand by the county, nonstructural improvements within easement areas (e.g., walkways, landscaping, etc.) are subject to immediate removal at the owner's risk and sole cost. The county shall not be liable for repairing, maintaining, or replacing (or otherwise reimbursing any person for) any item or improvement within the easement area that is removed to access, protect, repair, operate, or maintain the water system.
(b) No permanent structures shall be constructed within ten feet of the edge of a permanent water easement on front and rear setbacks, or within two feet on side setbacks. The department director may grant a variance, in writing, to this requirement, provided that it can be demonstrated to his reasonable satisfaction that such structure will not impede future installation, maintenance, replacement and other activities relating to the county water system within said easement.
(Code 1987, § 13-7; Ord. No. 2013-007, § I, 12-3-2013)
859:
All water service connections for which service has been discontinued as a result of the demolition of the structure being served by the connection, or for any other reasons, shall be properly and permanently capped and sealed to prevent the escape of potable water as required by the department director.
(Code 1987, § 13-8; Ord. No. 2013-007, § I, 12-3-2013)
860:
(a) It shall be unlawful for any person intentionally and without authority to:
(1) Damage, tamper with, alter, or destroy any meter, pipe, conduit, wire, line, or other part of the county water system;
(2) Prevent a meter from properly registering the quantity of water supplied;
(3) Divert or use (or cause to be used) water from the county water system without the required permit or payment of all scheduled fees and charges; or
(4) Otherwise interfere with the proper operation of the county water system.
(b) Where there is no evidence to the contrary, the person performing any of the illegal acts described in this section and the person who with knowledge of such violation receives the benefit of such service without proper charge shall be presumed to be responsible for such acts of tampering or diversion.
(c) Any person who violates subsection (a) of this section, upon citation and conviction of the violation in a court of competent jurisdiction, shall, in addition to civil and other penalties and remedies authorized in this chapter, be subject to imprisonment as provided in section 1-8. Where any offense or violation continues from day to day, each day's continuance thereof shall be deemed a separate offense.
(d) In addition to fines and other criminal and civil penalties and remedies authorized hereunder, any person convicted for violation of this section shall pay retribution to the county for any damage to its equipment at current costs for labor and materials necessary to reestablish service and otherwise repair and replace damage portions of the county water system.
(e) Any person negligently damaging or destroying any portion of the county water system shall also be liable for the full repair and replacement cost, as the case may be, of said damaged or destroyed components.
(Code 1987, § 13-9; Ord. No. 2013-007, § I, 12-3-2013)
861:
It shall be unlawful for any person to physically interconnect a private well or other private water supply with the county water system, whether separated by shutoff values, backflow preventers, or any other device, and irrespective of the quality or characteristics of water in the private supply system.
(Code 1987, § 13-10; Ord. No. 2013-007, § I, 12-3-2013)
862:
(a) The county shall make every reasonable effort to provide continuous service and potable water. The county does not warrant that system malfunctions or deficiencies will not result in service interruptions or pressure changes, nor does it guarantee that water quality will not vary, nor does it guarantee that it will be directly suitable for special commercial or industrial processes. The county assumes no liability for damages caused by varying pressure, interrupted service or water quality changes.

The department director shall endeavor to give public notice in the event of water shortage or prolonged routine maintenance interruptions of service.
